title: Production 5xx surge caused by retry-throttle feedback loop; investigation and hotpatch
creator: Laura Mitchell
description:
Summary: During a period of elevated traffic on 2025-03-11 we started receiving widespread 5xx errors and client timeouts for multiple customers on the Hosted API. Initial triage showed retries from SDK clients combined with an aggressive adaptive throttling change introduced in runtime-1.18 created a feedback loop that overloaded a subset of serving pools. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigations, hotpatch, and follow-up work to prevent recurrence.

Observed behavior: 1) Elevated 5xx rate (502/503) on a fraction (~12%) of host GPU pools. 2) Increased p95 latency and request timeouts leading to client-side retries. 3) Retry storms amplified load because throttling moved to aggressive rejections rather than smooth backoff.

Root cause hypothesis: Interaction between the new adaptive throttle algorithm (switch to reject-heavy policy under transient overload) and client retry behavior produced rapid oscillation. A subset of nodes had degraded KV-cache hit rates due to an ongoing cache-eviction regression; that caused higher per-request cost and longer tail latency which triggered the throttle.

Immediate mitigation implemented: 1) Rolled back adaptive-throttle alpha flag for hosted; 2) Deployed per-tenant circuit-breaker with exponential backoff for SDK traffic; 3) Applied hotpatch to revert cache-eviction tuning (PR linked below) on affected pools; 4) Increased request queue depth and enforced affinity for KV-cache local shards.

Permanent actions planned: 1) Add end-to-end test for cache-eviction and KV-affinity under load. 2) Rework adaptive throttle to consider KV-latency signals and not only rejection rate. 3) Improve SDK client backoff recommendations and server-side tenant-aware rate limiting. 4) Create dashboard alerts for early detection of throttle-retry feedback loops.

Related artifacts: runbook, dashboards, PRs and customer communications are linked in comments below.
